title: Day 5 Teaching Lab — From Threat Model to Incident Improvement
objective: Study-guide review — Day 5 — Threat Modeling, Monitoring, Hunting, and Incident Response: Day 5 Teaching Lab — From Threat Model to Incident Improvement.

blocks.text: Scenario: a public web application begins making unusual DNS requests. Web logs show suspicious parameters. Endpoint telemetry shows the web service spawning a shell. Identity logs show no administrator login. A threat feed contains one matching domain, but the domain appeared after the first suspicious request.
Ask students to produce five artifacts:

rows: Attack surface, likely input path, affected assets, assumptions
Web logs, endpoint process data, DNS logs, identity logs, cloud/application logs
Injection or command execution hypothesis, least-privilege review
First suspicious request, process execution, DNS activity, containment, recovery
Secure coding fix, detection update, logging gap, tabletop/playbook change

items: The threat feed is supporting intelligence, not the only evidence.
The absence of administrator login does not rule out application-layer compromise.
DNS activity becomes more meaningful when tied to process telemetry.
Root cause must address input handling, privilege, patching, and monitoring.
Recovery should include evidence preservation and validation before return to service.

blocks.text: Wrong-answer discussion: "block the domain and close the incident" treats an indicator as the root cause. SecurityX-level response requires timeline, cause, containment, eradication, recovery, and improvement.
Source: CertMaster Study Lessons 5A-5E; SecurityX M05 slides.
